blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication preparation for enteral feeding tubes
stem: Before crushing a solid oral medication for administration through an enteral feeding tube, what should the nurse verify first?

options.A: Verify that the exact dosage form is suitable for manipulation and tube administration before crushing or opening the product.
options.B: Verify that enteral nutrition is running because solid oral medications become safe to crush once tube feeding has started.
options.C: Verify that the tablet is small enough to pass through the tube because tablet size determines whether crushing is appropriate.
options.D: Verify that the medication has little taste because palatability determines whether an oral dosage form can be safely crushed.

rationale: A is correct. Enteral-medication guidance states that the specific dosage form must be evaluated for suitability before manipulation; some modified-release and enteric-coated products are inappropriate to crush or otherwise alter. B is incorrect because feeding status does not make an unsuitable dosage form safe to crush. C is incorrect because dosage-form design, not tablet size alone, determines whether manipulation is appropriate. D is incorrect because taste is not the safety criterion for crushing.
educational_objective: Verify the suitability of the exact oral dosage form before crushing a medication for enteral-tube administration, especially modified-release and enteric-coated products.
source_organization: American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (ASPEN) / Journal of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition; National Library of Medicine; NCSBN
source_document_title: Developing guidance for feeding tube administration of oral medications; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: JPEN 2023; PubMed current record rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: Klang 2023 PubMed abstract: physical evaluation of oral medications for appropriateness for feeding-tube administration; some products identified as inappropriate. Review article PubMed 19052281: before solid dosage forms are given through feeding tubes, determine whether the medication is suitable for manipulation such as crushing or opening a capsule.
source_claim_supported: Authoritative enteral-medication literature supports checking product-specific dosage-form suitability before manipulation and recognizes modified-release/enteric-coated formulations as common noncrushable forms.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: evaluate medication orders, prepare/administer medications safely, and review pertinent data before administration.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; medication-manipulation claims rely on current PubMed-indexed guidance.

option_audit.A: Correct; product-specific dosage-form suitability is the first safety question.
option_audit.B: Plausible feeding-timing concern but does not establish crushability.
option_audit.C: Plausible mechanical concern but tablet size does not determine whether formulation alteration is safe.
option_audit.D: Plausible administration-comfort concern but taste is not the crushability criterion.

cueing_audit.answer_length: Options are comparable in length and structure; the key is not uniquely signaled.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
